NO HOTSPOT. The largest self-time symbol is 4.38%. Twelve symbols sit between
1.9% and 4.4% and nothing towers. If you are looking for an O(n^2) regression,
it is not here.

BUT THE SYMBOLS CLUSTER, and that is the reading the flat list hides:

    memory management   ~18.7%   malloc/_int_malloc/_int_free/memmove, by full
                                 stack; libc.so.6 alone is 20.5% SELF time
    transcendentals      ~9.7%   libm exp 4.11 + pow 2.96 + sin 2.67
    noise                 4.2%   Fbm::sample
    routing               3.5%   topology::route::least_cost

THE ACTIONABLE PART. Attributing allocator samples to their deepest hornvale
frame:

     2.35%   observed_phenomena_from_with_climate
     0.86%   phenomena_sources_from
     0.63%   species::biosphere_registry
     0.44%   topology::route::least_cost

`observed_phenomena_from_with_climate` runs PER OBSERVATION — one per
settlement, per world — and its body reads:

    let boxed = phenomena_sources_from(world, climate)?;
    let sources: Vec<&dyn PhenomenaSource> = boxed.iter().map(|s| s.as_ref()).collect();

Three `Box` allocations and a `Vec` of three references, rebuilt every call.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH SOMEONE'S TIME IS THE HISTORY. A prior campaign already
optimised this exact seam — `observed_phenomena_as_at_from`'s doc says it
reuses an ALREADY-BUILT climate "instead of once per place", because deriving
one runs the full terrain-sculpting pipeline. That fix hoisted the EXPENSIVE
thing out of the loop and left the cheap thing in it. The cheap thing is now
3.2% of a census, and it is visible only because the expensive thing is gone.

TWO CAUTIONS FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT:
  - the sources borrow from `world` and `climate`, so hoisting them past the
    per-observation boundary may be a genuine lifetime problem rather than a
    five-line change.
  - this path is documented as BYTE-IDENTICAL to `observed_phenomena_as_at`.
    Any change owes a `cmp` of seed-42 output before it is believed, not a
    green suite — see the standing rule that byte-identity is not a perf proof
    and perf is not a byte-identity proof.
